verdict.rationale: OpenCode documents a one-shot `opencode run "<prompt>"` CLI invocation and an `--auto` flag that auto-approves permission requests, so it can run unattended in scripts. It also offers a headless `opencode serve` server and execution inside GitHub Actions runners, which shows it is built for workflow automation. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that `run` is non-interactive, including output formats, exit codes and scripting flags, plus independent hands-on corroboration of scripted or CI usage.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the agent non-interactively in scripts for workflow automation

citations.quote: opencode run "Explain how closures work in JavaScript"
Start OpenCode with `--auto` to automatically approve permission requests that are not explicitly denied.
The opencode serve command runs a headless HTTP server that exposes an OpenAPI endpoint that an opencode client can use.
OpenCode will execute tasks within your GitHub Actions runner.
